clue.text: Likely to make horse noises?

parts.note: a pun: someone with a rasping, croaky throat sounds like a neighing animal, and the adjective for that throat sounds like the animal's name

explanation.surface: A question about whether something is apt to neigh.
explanation.definitionFit: A rough, croaky voice is one that grates like a neigh, and the word for it sounds like the stable animal.

clue.text: Temporary commission always turned up to hearten a baronet

indicators.note: to hearten is to put something into the heart of the baronet's abbreviation
in a down clue, turned up means the word for always is read from bottom to top

parts.note: always means ever

explanation.surface: An officer's temporary promotion, perpetually raised to cheer an aristocrat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' reverses EVER to REVE, and 'to hearten' places it inside BT, the abbreviation for a baronet.
explanation.definitionFit: A brevet is an army commission giving an officer a higher rank, often temporarily, without the matching pay.

clue.text: Inability to distinguish flags containing blends in variegation

indicators.note: the word for flags is said to contain, so it wraps around the rest

parts.note: a regiment's flags are its colours

indicators.note: variegation is a mixing of colours, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A description of failing to tell banners apart when their hues merge together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variegation' (a mixing of colours) is the anagram signal, and 'in' belongs to the fodder rather than linking; 'containing' wraps the flags around the shuffled letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The condition is a failure to tell certain hues apart, so the definition names the impairment loosely.

clue.text: Continue with the ironing

definitions.meaning: to continue is to carry on or proceed despite difficulty
literally, to push the iron down onto the cloth when ironing

explanation.surface: Advice to carry on with the household chores.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means to persevere, and literally describes pushing an iron onto fabric.

clue.text: Icy world event RA represents

indicators.note: to represent here is to re-present, setting the same letters out afresh

explanation.surface: A Royal Academy painting depicts a frozen global occurrence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'represents' rearranges ICY WORLD EVENT RA, all fifteen letters, and the whole clue also describes the answer: a frozen season.
explanation.definitionFit: A bitterly cold season is a freezing event across the world, which the whole clue describes.

clue.text: Seabird under wooden tile one that makes the house untidy

definitions.text: one that makes the house untidy

indicators.note: in a down clue, the seabird goes under the tile, so it comes after it

parts.note: a slat is a thin strip of wood, like a tile
a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: A gull perched beneath a roof shingle, with someone causing household mess.
explanation.definitionFit: A slattern is an old word for a slovenly woman who keeps a dirty, messy home.

clue.text: Discourteous claim to Slav citizenship includes it

indicators.note: the claim is said to include the next word, so it goes inside

parts.note: a Polish person might claim 'I'm Pole', a Pole being a Slav

explanation.surface: A rude assertion of Slavic nationality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'includes' puts IT inside I'M POLE, a Slav's claim to be from Poland.
explanation.definitionFit: Being discourteous means lacking good manners, which is the plain sense of the answer.

clue.text: Common time for tea for two?

definitions.text: Common time for tea for two?

parts.words: Common time for tea for two?
parts.note: musical common time has four beats to the bar; the joke reads 'for' and 'two' as numbers in the song title

explanation.surface: A question about the usual hour for a couple's afternoon tea.
explanation.definitionFit: Common time in music is the time signature with four crotchet beats per bar.

clue.text: Book turned up by the hard of hearing

definitions.meaning: a book is a single tome, one of a set

definitions.text: turned up by the hard of hearing
definitions.meaning: people who hear badly raise the loudness on the radio or television

explanation.surface: A deaf reader's book being raised.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a bound tome and loudness, which the deaf turn up.

clue.text: The day before there was only Adam

definitions.meaning: the evening or day before a festival, as on Christmas
before the first woman was made, Adam was alone in Eden

explanation.surface: A Bible-flavoured note about the time before Creation was complete.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means the eve of an event, and names the first woman, before whom Adam was alone.

clue.text: Prior is a parson in godly surroundings

indicators.note: the parson is placed in the other word
the godly word forms the surroundings, enclosing the cleric

parts.note: godly means pious
a parson is a clergyman, Rev for Reverend

explanation.surface: A monastery's prior is a clergyman living among the devout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in ... surroundings' signals the container. 'Prior' looks like a monk, fitting the parson, but here it is the adjective meaning earlier.
explanation.definitionFit: Prior as an adjective means earlier or preceding in time.

clue.text: Limit relative magnitude to a point

parts.note: a ratio is the relative size of two quantities
N, north, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: An instruction to restrict a comparative size to one spot.
explanation.definitionFit: To ration something is to limit how much of it each person gets.

clue.text: IOU travellers present to banks

parts.note: documents a bank issues so travellers can draw money from banks abroad, a kind of promise to pay

explanation.surface: Tourists handing promissory notes over the counter.
explanation.definitionFit: These are bank documents guaranteeing payment, once carried by travellers to obtain cash abroad.

clue.text: Play with alphabet up to but not including Z

parts.note: up to is the word to, as in A to Z
the alphabet stopping short of Z ends on the letter before it, Y

explanation.surface: Fiddling with the alphabet but stopping one letter short.
explanation.walkthrough: The alphabet run not quite A to Z is A to Y, and the last part, to Y, gives the answer; 'alphabet' sets the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: To toy with something is to play with it idly.

clue.text: No damp dungeon, despite its delivering a charge of battery

definitions.meaning: literally a prison cell that is not wet
a type of electric battery with a paste electrolyte that delivers charge

explanation.surface: A dry prison cell, though someone there is charged with assault.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an electric battery with non-liquid electrolyte, and literally a dungeon that isn't damp.

clue.text: Radical short cut to vegetables

parts.note: radical comes from Latin for root
to crop is to cut short

explanation.surface: A drastic trim applied to greens.
explanation.definitionFit: Carrots, turnips and the like are crops grown for their edible underground parts.

clue.text: Crossword monger translating into machine code

definitions.meaning: the setter who puts a crossword together
a program that converts source code into instructions a computer runs

explanation.surface: A puzzle setter who works in computer language.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is the setter of a crossword, and the software that converts code for a machine.

clue.text: Islander beheaded for defamation of character

indicators.note: beheaded means the first letter of the word is cut off

explanation.surface: An island dweller decapitated for libel.
explanation.definitionFit: Slander is spoken defamation that damages someone's reputation.

clue.text: The sort of cheque that may be returned

indicators.note: the word reads the same when returned, read backwards, as a bounced cheque is returned

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A remark about a bad cheque sent back by the bank.
explanation.walkthrough: Double play: a worthless cheque is sent back unpaid, and its three-letter name reads the same either way.
explanation.definitionFit: A dud cheque is a worthless one that bounces.

clue.text: Endlessly the fellow supports a son of Judah

indicators.note: in a down clue the fellow sits beneath the son, holding him up

parts.note: Onan is a son of Judah in Genesis
a don is a university fellow

explanation.surface: A man helps hold up a biblical figure.
explanation.definitionFit: On and on means continuously, without stopping.

clue.text: Everyone is aware of what students of public land need

definitions.meaning: facts that everyone is aware of

definitions.text: what students of public land need
definitions.meaning: learning about shared public land, a village green, is literally knowledge of the common

explanation.surface: What everyone knows, and what students of shared land must have.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means facts known to everyone; a common is public land.

clue.text: It provides a pupil with blinking protection

definitions.text: It provides a pupil with blinking protection

parts.words: It provides a pupil with blinking protection
parts.note: the pupil is of the eye, not a schoolchild, and blinking is literal, not a mild swear word

explanation.surface: Something giving a schoolchild ruddy good protection.
explanation.definitionFit: The fold of skin over the eye closes in a blink, shielding the pupil.

clue.text: One suffering from fag!

parts.note: fag means exhaustion, which leaves one panting; fag is also slang for a cigarette, and so is the answer

explanation.surface: Someone worn out, or a smoker's complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: A gasper is someone panting from fatigue, and old slang for a cheap cigarette.

clue.text: Court case in which men at the front take part

definitions.text: in which men at the front take part
definitions.meaning: soldiers at the front line see combat

explanation.surface: A legal case involving front-line soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a lawsuit and military combat.

clue.text: Only …W, then the other points amount to absurdity

parts.note: only west means no north, south or east: NO plus N, S and E
the compass points other than west are N, S and E

explanation.surface: A cryptic compass instruction that adds up to rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: Having only W means having NO N, S, E; then the other points again, NSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Nonsense is talk or ideas without sense, absurdity.

clue.text: Not A side to finish off

definitions.meaning: the ... of a field or box are not its sides
to finish off is to conclude

explanation.surface: A team other than the first eleven, ready to wrap things up.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names an extremity, as opposed to a side, and the act of concluding.

clue.text: Way manuscript can be transmitted by computer links

parts.note: a way of doing something is a mode

explanation.surface: How a writer's draft can be sent electronically.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can be transmitted by' joins the wordplay to the definition, with the whole clue describing how the devices carry a manuscript.
explanation.definitionFit: These devices link computers through telephone lines, modulating and demodulating signals.

clue.text: Biased description of a Moebius strip

definitions.meaning: a Moebius strip is a twisted loop with only one surface

explanation.surface: A partial account of a mathematical curiosity.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means partial, and literally describes a surface with a single face.
